dbdb04bb.task:
Black-box reconnaissance of in-scope WordPress target https://dkv.smkn1-pkp.sch.id/

Goal: fingerprint the exact WordPress core version, active theme and version, installed plugins and versions, and map the WP attack surface. Report concrete version strings and endpoint inventory. Do NOT exploit or spray injection payloads yet — recon only.

Perform these checks (use curl/httpx/wpscan if available, and Caido proxy via HTTP_PROXY is already set):

1. WordPress core version:
   - GET / (read HTML: <meta name="generator" content="WordPress X.Y.Z">, wp-content asset query strings ?ver=, wp-includes/js/wp-embed.min.js or any /wp-includes/js/* ?ver=)
   - GET /feed/ and check generator tag in RSS
   - GET /readme.html (many versions expose "Version X.Y.Z")
   - GET /wp-includes/version.php is not directly readable but try; more reliable: static file hashes if wpscan enumerates
   - GET /wp-login.php and inspect login page, CSS ver strings, any version leakage
2. Theme enumeration:
   - GET /wp-content/themes/ (directory listing if enabled)
   - Parse HTML for active theme path (wp-content/themes/<slug>/...)
   - Check active theme style.css (GET /wp-content/themes/<slug>/style.css) for "Theme Name" and "Version" header, and readme.txt / changelog.txt in theme dir
   - Enumerate known theme slugs with ffuf if time permits (bounded)
3. Plugin enumeration:
   - Parse HTML/JS for wp-content/plugins/<slug>/ paths
   - GET /wp-content/plugins/ (directory listing if enabled)
   - For each discovered plugin, GET its readme.txt (stable tag / changelog / version), style.css, or main plugin file header to determine version
   - Run ffuf bounded scan against a common WP plugin wordlist to discover additional plugin slugs (target path /wp-content/plugins/FUZZ/)
   - Cross-reference discovered plugins with known vulnerable versions (note CVE candidates, but only list them)
4. WP attack surface inventory:
   - GET /xmlrpc.php (POST system.listMethods) to confirm enabled and list methods
   - GET /wp-json/ (REST index) and /wp-json/wp/v2/ routes
   - GET /wp-json/wp/v2/users and /wp-json/wp/v2/users?per_page=100 — enumerate usernames/IDs/slugs
   - GET /wp-login.php, /wp-admin/ (redirect behavior), /wp-signup.php
   - Check /wp-cron.php, /wp-links-opml.php, /?p=1 etc if trivial
   - Note any exposed uploads dir, debug.log (/wp-content/debug.log), backup files (wp-config.php.bak, .git, .svn) — only detect presence, do not download sensitive content beyond confirming existence
5. Server/technology headers: capture response headers (Server, X-Powered-By, etc.), note WAF presence if any.

Be careful to stay on the in-scope host only. Output a structured report to the parent: exact core version, theme name+version, each plugin name+version+slug+confirmed URL, xmlrpc status+methods, REST users list, and any CVE candidates you can identify (with CVE IDs) for the versions found. Also list any interesting files/dirs discovered. Do not send exploit payloads or test injection in this phase.

3. Check for local nuclei CVE templates: `find / -path '*nuclei-templates*' -type d 2>/dev/null` and `find / -iname '*.yaml' -path '*elementor*' 2>/dev/null`, same for pagelayer/loginpress/wpforms/the-post-grid/astra. List any templates matching these slugs/CVEs.

Be precise: do NOT invent CVE IDs. If a product shows no CVE in local data, say "none found". Sort output by exploitability/likelihood (prefer pre-auth/unauthenticated, then low-priv authenticated). This output drives the validation phase, so include the concrete attack vector (endpoint + parameter) for the top candidates, especially Elementor Pro 3.7.5 and PageLayer 2.2.2.
